literal: Even by besieging, or without besieging by attacking, or even by undermining from within, to capture difficult is a fortress.
translation: A true fortress is one that is impossible to capture, whether by laying a long siege, by launching a sudden direct assault, or by attempting to undermine it through internal treachery.
modern: முற்றுகையிட்டோ, முற்றுகையிடாமல் திடீரென்று தாக்கியோ, அல்லது உள்ளிருப்பவர்களை வஞ்சனையால் வசப்படுத்தியோ கைப்பற்றுவதற்கு அரியதே சிறந்த அரணாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate strength of a fortress by listing the three primary methods used to capture one. 'Muṟṟiyum' refers to surrounding the fort in a prolonged siege to starve the defenders. 'Muṟṟātu eṟintum' refers to bypassing a siege and launching an immediate, aggressive storming of the walls. 'Aṟaippaṭuttum' refers to the act of bribing or deceiving those inside to betray the fort from within. A perfect fortress (araṇ) is one that remains impregnable (paṟṟaṟku ariyatu) against all three of these tactics.
